community: Remote & backcountry, Peace River Regional District

description.value: A remote wilderness camp associated with Kakwa Park, set amid ice-clad peaks and alpine meadows near the Continental Divide; reaching it demands roughly 100 km on a rutted, 4x4-only forest service road, and no potable water is available.

raw_osm.name: Lower Horse Camp
raw_osm.source: hand drawn map at info sign near Kakwa Lake ranger cabin

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies Lower Horse Camp as a backcountry campsite within Kakwa Park, sourced from a hand-drawn map at an info sign near Kakwa Lake ranger cabin — it is not named anywhere on the BC Parks website. The website explicitly states 'Potable water is not available at the park' and describes extremely remote access (~100km from staging site via rough 4x4 road). The camp name 'Lower Horse Camp' signals an equestrian primary use; while mountain bikes are permitted on the Tote Road to Kakwa Lake, 'any other trail within the park' prohibits mountain bikes and e-bikes.
concerns: Lower Horse Camp is not mentioned by name anywhere on the BC Parks Kakwa Park website; the OSM record is sourced solely from a hand-drawn map at an on-site info sign.
The camp name strongly implies primary equestrian use, which may not align with cycling tourism directory inclusion.
Extremely remote location (~100km from staging area, no potable water, 4x4 access road only) limits practical utility for most touring cyclists.
The website provided covers all of Kakwa Park and contains no site-specific information for Lower Horse Camp; many amenity fields cannot be verified.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Lower Horse Camp is primarily an equestrian backcountry site with no named presence on the BC Parks website, no potable water, and access requiring ~100km of rough 4x4 road from the staging area. It may be relevant for highly adventurous bikepacking expeditions using the Tote Road corridor, but is unlikely to serve typical touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: Mountain bikes are permitted on the Tote Road from the park boundary to Kakwa Lake (Class 1 e-bikes also permitted on this segment only). All other trails within the park prohibit mountain bikes and e-bikes. This access detail is relevant context if the listing is included for bikepacking audiences.
